label: input 2 after j/n (preceded by j/c) mid-prefix, sparse token-combination feature
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.005% of steps). It fires only in the original phase at t=3-6 (most at t=4), plus a little on <DEL>, and never in the copy phase. It seems to respond to a specific combination of prefix tokens: the strongest activations are input 2 coming after a run of j/n/c in sequences that start with b (also d or 3), e.g. b c j n [2]. Input 2 holds about 66% of the activation mass, prev_tok j/n holds about 74%, prev2_tok j/c about 74%, and first_tok b about 66%. In the examples, magnitude is higher when more of these tokens are present (b first, c, j and n all before the 2); that was read off the examples, not measured. No single conjunction separates it well. The best predicate (2 after j/n after j/c at t>=3) gets dev F1 0.26 and mass recall 0.31. Adding first_tok in {b,d,3} raises precision to 0.81 but recall falls to 0.07. Many activations occur on other tokens (y, r, c, <DEL>) that follow the same b..j..n context, and many 2-after-j/n steps in sequences not starting with b/d/3 do not fire. This looks like a hidden-state conjunction of several remembered prefix tokens, which these predicates do not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 39 cues. Raise it: orig0=b (+4.63), prev_tok=n (+2.87), prev2_tok=j (+2.54), orig0=d (+2.38), prev_tok=j (+2.31), orig1=c (+1.97). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-1.84), phase=2 (-1.72), prev3_tok=b (-1.23), orig_idx=-1 (-0.57).
